Issues.Title: Add DataGridView edit mode tests
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

- `DataGridView` edit mode had almost no direct coverage beyond a couple of `CellEndEdit`/`EditMode` checks. This adds `DataGridViewTests.Editing.cs` with tests for entering and leaving edit mode.
- Covers `BeginEdit`, `EndEdit`, `CancelEdit` and `CommitEdit`: no-op behavior when not editing, no current cell, read-only and non-editable cells, and `CellBeginEdit` cancellation.
- Covers commit/cancel semantics and event order, dirty state, `CurrentCell` changes while editing (including canceled validation), editing control reuse and `EditingControlShowing` style changes, combo box and check box cells, parse failures raising `DataError`, data-bound commit/cancel, and the custom `IDataGridViewEditingControl` contract.
- Test-only change. No product code is modified.

## Customer Impact

- None. Test-only; guards edit mode behavior against regressions.

## Regression?

- No

## Risk

- Minimal. New tests only.

## Validation

- `.\build.cmd -configuration Debug` succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- `System.Windows.Forms.Tests.exe --filter-class "System.Windows.Forms.Tests.DataGridViewTests"` run five times in a row: 859/859 passed each time.

Issues.Title: Add DataGridView selection mode and current cell tests
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

- Add `DataGridViewTests.Selection.cs` with 38 test cases (including theory data rows) covering `DataGridView` selection, which had very little direct coverage.
- Cover each `SelectionMode` with `MultiSelect` on and off: how `CurrentCell`, `Cell/Row/Column.Selected`, `SelectAll` and `ClearSelection` drive `SelectedCells`/`SelectedRows`/`SelectedColumns`.
- Cover the negative and constraint cases: `Selected` ignored in modes that don't support it, `Selected` before a band is added, `FullColumnSelect` with automatic sort columns, invalid mode values, hidden cells as current cell, hiding/removing the current or selected rows and columns, read-only cells.
- Cover event behavior: `CurrentCellChanged`/`SelectionChanged` counts and the leave/`SelectionChanged`/enter ordering when the current cell moves.
- No product code changes.

## Customer Impact

Issues.Title: CheckBox and RadioButton render incorrectly when AutoCheck is false
Issues.Body: ### Description When `AutoCheck` is set to `false`, clicking a `CheckBox` or `RadioButton` causes rendering artifacts: - The control's border is rendered incorrectly. - The `RadioButton` also displays an extra small circle. Reproduce on .NET Framework and .NET Core 3.1 through .NET 12. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a Windows Forms app with a `CheckBox` and a `RadioButton`. 2. Set `AutoCheck = false` on both controls. 3. Run the app and click each control. 4. Observe the rendering artifacts. ### Screenshots https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a120cff4-497e-470e-b38a-ae539bcd064b

Issues.Title: Fix Issue 12866: TabControl doesn't send the name of selected tab to accessibility clients on initial focus
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #12866


## Proposed changes

- Updated `TabControlAccessibleObject` to return the correct focused accessibility provider by using native `TCM_GETCURFOCUS`.
- Added focus handling to correctly distinguish between the focused tab and the selected tab when they differ.
- Kept `UIA_HasKeyboardFocusPropertyId` consistent with the object returned by `GetFocus()`.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Fixes an accessibility issue where Narrator announced only "tab control" when a `TabControl` initially received focus instead of announcing the focused tab name.
- Ensures the UIA focus provider correctly represents the focused tab item, improving screen reader behavior and accessibility compliance.

## Regression? 

- Yes

## Risk

- Low. The change is isolated to `TabControlAccessibleObject` focus reporting logic and does not modify the native focus behavior of `TabControl`. Added accessibility tests cover focused, selected, created, uncreated, and empty control scenarios.

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->


## Screenshots <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

### Before

<!-- TODO -->

When Narrator is running and focus moves to a `TabControl`, it announces only "tab control" because the accessibility provider reports the container as focused and does not return a focused child provider.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cb5eccc-608c-4fe7-9c99-887e51e64fd2

### After

<!-- TODO -->

When Narrator is running and focus moves to a `TabControl`, it correctly announces the focused tab item (for example, "Tab 1" or "Tab 2") because the accessibility provider returns the appropriate focused tab accessibility object.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72ffb9ef-c676-4811-aa9c-9733c828b240

## Test methodology <!-- How did you ensure quality? -->

- Added tests validating scenarios where the focused tab differs from the selected tab for both button-style tab appearances.
- Added validation that an empty focused `TabControl` reports itself as the focused accessibility object.
- Added tests verifying that uncreated controls return `null` without creating handles and that created but unfocused controls also return `null`.
- Added tests to verify that `UIA_HasKeyboardFocusPropertyId` remains consistent with the object returned from `GetFocus()`.
- Validated correct accessibility focus reporting when the `TabControl` receives focus while Narrator is running.

Issues.Title: Wrap DrawImageAbort in a BOOL-returning native callback
Issues.Body:
## Proposed changes

- `System.Drawing.Common` sets `[assembly: DisableRuntimeMarshalling]`, but the three `Graphics.DrawImage` overloads that take a `DrawImageAbort` pass the public delegate directly to `Marshal.GetFunctionPointerForDelegate`. `DrawImageAbort` returns `bool`, which isn't blittable.
- Since dotnet/runtime#130239, ILC builds reverse P/Invoke stubs for delegates from `DisableRuntimeMarshalling` assemblies from their managed signature. As a result, any NativeAOT app that roots these overloads gets `IL1005` on `System.Drawing.Graphics.DrawImageAbort`. Rooting can happen indirectly, for example through `DrawImage(Image, Rectangle, int, int, int, int, GraphicsUnit, ImageAttributes)`. With `IlcTreatWarningsAsErrors`, that warning becomes a build break.
- The callback now goes through a private `DrawImageAbortAdapter`, which uses a `BOOL`-returning native delegate. It mirrors the existing `EnumerateMetafileDataAdapter`. This also matches the native `ImageAbort` signature, which returns a 4-byte `BOOL`, instead of returning a 1-byte `bool`.

## Related

- ILC change that surfaced this: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/130239
- Companion fix for the same `IL1005` on `ConsoleCtrlHandlerRoutine` in `Microsoft.Win32.SystemEvents`: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/138178

## Customer Impact

- NativeAOT apps that reference `System.Drawing.Common` and use `Graphics.DrawImage` with `ImageAttributes` or a callback fail to publish when ILC warnings are treated as errors, starting with .NET 11.
- The workaround is to avoid the affected overloads or GDI+ altogether.

## Regression? 

- Yes. This is a regression with .NET 11 ILC (dotnet/runtime#130239).

## Risk

- Low. No public API changes. The change follows an existing pattern in the same type, and the null callback path still passes `0`.

## Test methodology

- No new tests. The existing test suite runs on CoreCLR, which doesn't reproduce the ILC diagnostic. The callback overloads keep their current behavior and are covered by existing `DrawImage` tests through the null-callback path.
- Found in a NativeAOT product build (`IL1005` on `DrawImageAbort`).

4. Set numericUpDown1.Value = numericUpDown1.Minimum in the second button’s click event.
5. Run the application and click the first button. The displayed text clears.

Issues.Body: Fixes #15438 ## Root Cause In Net11 mode, the button renderers rely on `ShouldSerializeBackColor()` to determine whether to use `BackColor`. After `ResetBackColor()`, that check returns false even when the effective color is inherited from the parent. Setting `BackColor` also disables `UseVisualStyleBackColor`, and that explicit opt-out remains in effect after the reset. ## Proposed changes - Make `ShouldSerializeUseVisualStyleBackColor()` available to the button renderers within the assembly. - In the Net11 color-selection paths, honor the effective `BackColor` when visual-style backgrounds have been explicitly disabled. Buttons that merely inherit a color without either setting being changed continue to use the theme color. - Add coverage for resetting an explicitly set `BackColor` on Standard, Flat and Popup buttons. ## Customer Impact - Net11 buttons, including CheckBox and RadioButton controls with `Appearance.Button`, can now display their inherited background color after `ResetBackColor()`, consistent with Classic mode for this scenario. ## Regression? - No. ## Risk - Minimal: the change is limited to the background-color decision in two renderers. The existing regression tests for dotnet/winforms#14778 continue to pass. ## Screenshots ### Before The form has a pink background. In the left column, Net11 Standard and Flat buttons remain at the neutral theme color at rest after their explicitly set backgrounds are reset; the Classic buttons on the right show the inherited pink. When clicked, Net11 buttons flash blue and Classic buttons darken slightly. These pressed-state colors are unrelated to the resting-color issue and are unchanged by this fix. ### After At rest, the Net11 buttons on the left now show the form's pink background, matching the unchanged Classic buttons on the right. Clicking still produces the same blue flash in Net11 and slight darkening in Classic as before. Issues.Title: Fix issue 15458: the mouse pointer is hidden while the user moves it over menus, drop-down lists and dialogs of the form
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15458 

## Root Cause

KioskModeManager detected mouse activity only from messages targeting the managed form or its child controls. Mouse messages for separate popup and owned windows were ignored.

When a modal dialog disabled the main form, mouse movement over the disabled form might not produce messages on the UI thread at all. As a result, the inactivity timer could hide the pointer while the user was moving it, and further movement might not restore it.

## Proposed changes

- Monitor mouse messages for windows on the same UI thread, including non-client mouse messages.
- Use a thread-specific message hook to observe messages in native modal loops and before other WinForms message filters can consume them.
- Periodically check the pointer position while fullscreen auto-hide is enabled, so movement can be detected even when no mouse message reaches the UI thread.
- Stop monitoring when auto-hide is disabled or fullscreen mode exits.
- Add regression tests for message routing, native modal loops, pointer movement, and monitoring lifecycle.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

The pointer remains visible while users move it over supported popup windows, owned forms, and modal dialogs. If it has been hidden, movement over a disabled main form can restore it.

The pointer-position check also detects movement over other applications or displays, which can restore the pointer and restart the inactivity timer.

I was unable to test earlier versions, but -to my amazement- everything works on .NET Framework 4.8. ### Issue description I'm testing some DPI-aware code, but am getting visual bugs when using anything besides `AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left`. On a 96 DPI (100%) monitor, I have a simple Form with a Panel control: ###### Figure 1: Starting layout at 100% DPI I will then move this Form to a 200% DPI monitor. If I have `panel.Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Left`, then I see what I would expect ###### Figure 2: Expected layout at 200% DPI When moving the Form back to the 100% DPI monitor, the panel remains in the correct position as well. However, other `AnchorStyles` cause problems... ###### Figure 3: `AnchorStyles.None` ###### Figure 4: `AnchorStyles.Top` ###### Figure 5: `AnchorStyles.Left` ###### Figure 6: `AnchorStyles.Right` ###### Figure 7: `AnchorStyles.Bottom` ###### Figure 8: `Top | Right` ###### Figure 9: `Top | Bottom` ###### Figure 10: `Left | Right` ###### Figure 11: `Left | Bottom` ###### Figure 12: `Bottom | Right` ###### Figure 13: `Top | Right | Bottom` ###### Figure 14: `Left | Right | Bottom` It's hard to tell in the images, but the sizes also get messed up a little bit. As well, when returning to the 100% DPI monitor, the bounds do not restore to their correct position, but instead become more divergent. The three remaining `AnchorStyles` configurations contain `Top | Left` and actually seem to work when moving to 200% DPI. However, in all three cases, when I move the Form back to the 100% DPI monitor, the width of the panel gets set to zero! * `Top | Left | Right` sets the width to zero * `Top | Left | Bottom` sets the height to zero * `Top | Left | Bottom | Right` sets both width and height to zero In all three cases, the the location seems to stay correct ### Steps to reproduce I've reduced the problem to this code sample: ```cs namespace WinFormsApp1; internal static class Program { /// /// The main entry point for the application. /// [STAThread] static void Main() { _ = Application.SetHighDpiMode(HighDpiMode.PerMonitorV2); Application.Run(new DpiTestForm()); } } class DpiTestForm : Form { private Panel panel; public DpiTestForm() { InitializeComponent(); } private void InitializeComponent() { panel = new Panel(); SuspendLayout(); // // panel // panel.Anchor = AnchorStyles.Top | AnchorStyles.Bottom; panel.Location = new Point(0, 0); panel.Size = new Size(150, 100); panel.BackColor = SystemColors.ControlDarkDark; // // Form1 // AutoScaleDimensions = new SizeF(96F, 96F); AutoScaleMode = AutoScaleMode.Dpi; ClientSize = new Size(250, 150); Controls.Add(panel); ResumeLayout(false); } } ``` And the .csproj file: ``` WinExe net10.0-windows true true ```
